answers.answer: Roll one die per held office card simultaneously, adding one for each fatigue on that card; the Chairman adds one more. Modified 1–2 has no effect, 3–4 adds fatigue, and 5+ retires the officeholder. Move the retiree to Pensioners, flip the card into Vacant Offices, and return its fatigue to supply.

Only players who retired at least one pensioner select or discard one display card. Order is descending actual total retirement spending; ties go to the most total windows, including new prizes, then clockwise from the PM. The acting player may peek at display blackmails. There is no immediate refill; if the display empties, remaining players are skipped. At the end discard remaining display cards and refill three even if nobody took one. Return unused pensioners to their supplies.

At phase start, if the opportunity marker is already on the chosen action, the player may take that action twice; otherwise take it once and place the marker there. Only the latest passed extra-action law is usable, and its extra action is not doubled and does not move the marker. With four vacant offices, Enlist Writer places one additional writer once that turn. Thus a doubled Enlist Writer action places three writers total.
answers.evidence: Family action rules and Enlist Writer row

answers.answer: After family actions, while Debt and applicants both remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one, repeating as possible. With no Debt, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible while preserving order. The initial share purchase price is paid to the bank; it does not go to Company treasuries.

Fill vacancies in ascending number on their card backs. Choosing your own family member requires verbal consent from every other player represented in that office's candidate pool. On promotion, transfer fatigue to the new card and insert the old card, vacant, into ascending hiring order. If there is no candidate or the hirer is vacant, skip the office; it stays vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.

The former Chairman announces support for a candidate from shareholders holding a pure majority of current Company shares (more than half); any shareholder may campaign, and the first candidate supported by players controlling that majority wins. If nobody reaches that support, the former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including themself, without Nepotism consent. The winner's Company share moves into the Chairman slot and remains a share for dividends, majority and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in firms.

Commit resources and cash, gather dice, subtract penalties, then roll and use the lowest die. A 1–2 succeeds; 3–4 fails and can be retried if resources and office limits allow; 5–6 is catastrophic, ends that office's actions, returns the officeholder to supply, discards fatigue, and flips the card into Vacant Offices. Specific Commander/firm procedures modify this. Do not take an action with no effect or chance of success (for example, trade with no ship or deploy with no dice to trigger possible officer losses).

The Chairman may add up to three Debt freely, each adding £5 to Balance. Each additional advance requires consent from players controlling a majority of Company shares, counting the Chairman; never advance past the Debt track end. The Chairman must allocate all Balance to other offices' treasuries, reducing Balance by each transfer. Borrowing and allocation may be interleaved while respecting the borrowing limits; cash already in office treasuries remains there.

Shipping must spend its treasury until £2 or less remains. It may lease an extra ship for £2, fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 without owner consent, or buy a Company ship for £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Place each acquired ship in any sea zone, including China once that office exists. Extra ships last only until Refresh.

Declare regions including the home region and only regions reachable through open orders with available ship capacity. Each £1 from the President's treasury buys one die; subtract one die per declared nonhome region. Failure may be retried if affordable; catastrophe removes the President. On success, fill one order per ship in its sea zone, as many as possible within declared regions, starting at the home port and extending through adjacent orders filled by that Presidency. Use actual writers while available, then filled-order tokens. A Presidency cannot fill another Presidency's home region even if that office is vacant. Add each filled order's printed value to Balance; the President receives £1 per order and writer owners receive £1 per writer placed. Each President may have at most one successful Trade per turn.

A Commander may target their Presidency's home region, any associated region, or a region bordering an associated region; they cannot target another home region or another Presidency's Company-controlled region. A Company region must have unrest or a closed order for the action to have an effect. Exhaust officers and regiments for one die each and local alliances for their printed dice; subtract target tower strength plus all strength of its empire, while Company-controlled defense strength is zero. After every attempt, each owner rolls one die per officer they exhausted in that attempt; each 6 removes that officer to supply. Regiments do not roll for losses.

On success, loot is £4 per target tower plus the faceup loot token modifier, with at least one plus the number of surviving used officers. Distribute £1 to the Commander plus £1 per their used surviving officer, then clockwise £1 per other player's used surviving officer, then £1 to the bank per regiment and per alliance piece, repeating the cycle until the cash is gone. The Commander gets one trophy per target tower. Remove the tower/dome, open all orders and clear unrest; if newly Company-controlled, place the control token, Governor overlay and office card among vacancies. On catastrophe, the Commander returns half their family's trophies rounded up and the Commander member to supply; exhausted officers still check losses.
answers.evidence: Commanders and Deploy — success and catastrophe

answers.answer: Take the printed dice pool. Each attempt rolls the current pool without penalty, then reduces the pool by one. Success pays the Governor £1, plus £1 if the previous roll was unsuccessful, and permits one choice: build or advance a Company ship, commission a regiment, or tax by adding an unsplit £2 to Balance or the President's treasury. Each Tax after the first this turn adds unrest. Each unsuccessful check adds unrest. Continue until choosing to stop, running out of dice, or catastrophe, which uses normal office removal.

Company expenses are paid first. If Balance is insufficient, take £5 emergency loans, advancing Debt one each until the track ends; continue receiving emergency loans at maximum Debt too. New emergency Debt adds no expense this turn. After using emergency loans, set Balance to zero. One or two loans lower Standing one; three or more lower it two. Then compare remaining Balance with expectations for current Standing and lower Standing one if Balance is below expectations. After that, the Chairman may pay any affordable dividends; if total dividend cash paid is strictly greater than expectations, raise Standing one.

An attack on a Company region also triggers secondary Rebellions in every other Company region with unrest. Resolve the primary attack first, then Bombay, Madras and Bengal; each Commander orders attacks in their Presidency. Primary strength uses the normal attack calculation plus local unrest; a secondary attack uses only that region's unrest. The associated Commander must exhaust active Army pieces totaling the attack strength, or as much as possible. If the exhausted strength is insufficient, the Company loses the region. Otherwise clear all unrest there and the Commander takes one trophy. If the Commander is vacant, Military Affairs chooses, then Chairman if Military Affairs is vacant; the substitute gets or loses no trophies.
answers.support: Events in India — Attacks on Company

answers.answer: A vote total/support of −1 or less fails: discard the law, resolve a dilemma's If Failed text, transfer the PM dial to the Opposition Leader, and have the new PM move the proposed policy one space in either direction and resolve that adjacent policy. At zero or higher the law passes: place it with passed laws, give the PM a passed-law token, resolve the selected policy, then resolve immediate law effects. Voting starts at the law's printed support; a round with no votes ends voting. If a law causes Company failure, finish the vote before scoring.

In 1758 and Long 1710, the PM may call the special vote at turn start before London Season if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is on a starred space. Passing reduces Debt by one per two current Debt, sets Standing to S, gives the PM a passed-law token and activates firms. Failing increases Company-share scoring value by flipping/placing a Court VP token, up to ±3. There is no policy attached; failure neither removes the PM nor discards the Deregulation law, and the PM may vote against. 1813 starts deregulated.

A player not already managing a firm may form one by returning an eligible Company share to supply or flipping a workshop to its invested side; flip the family board, place a family member as the first firm share, set value to the leftmost track space, and take £5 from the bank to the firm's London treasury. With the manager's consent, invest by the same share/workshop contribution to create a firm share and take £5 from the bank to London. A firm may have up to ten shares; further investments still add £5 but create no share. The Chairman share cannot be used. Company shares cannot be invested when Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, nor can shares created this turn be used. Invested workshops cannot be uninvested and no longer give bonuses or Company-failure VP; they remain invested even if the firm fails.

Each manager secretly selects a sea zone/home port and London cash bid, requiring at least one ship, or selects Hobnob with no bid (no trade or dividends, expenses still apply, and the prior dividend marker remains). At the associated Presidency's operation start, matching firms reveal and roll one die per bid pound, paying the bid to the bank; at least one 1 or 2 succeeds. Firm initiative is ship count minus successful dice. A successful President's Trade also establishes initiative. Following that success, fill orders from lowest initiative upward, with the President breaking ties. If the President is vacant or never successfully trades, firms fill after Commander/Governor opportunities and the Chairman breaks ties. A firm fills up to ships + 1 open orders, beginning at its home port and tracing its own route, once per order per firm; it may refill orders filled earlier this turn by another firm or Company. Previously filled orders pay half listed revenue, rounded down. Advance value one space per full £6 added to India treasury this turn.
answers.evidence: Deregulation — Firm strategies and competing trade

answers.answer: At Revenue start, firms pay £1 per charter ship plus the higher of share count or firm value, using either or both treasuries. If unable to pay, dissolve unless rescued: shareholders may make emergency investments under normal contribution rules (including the ten-share limit), paying expenses, losing remaining cash and lowering value one space per investment, or merge with one other firm that first pays its own expenses if needed and covers the unpaid expenses. Dissolution sends shares to Debtor's Prison for −1 VP each, returns ships to shipyards and flips the charter to the family side; workshops remain invested. After expenses the manager may pay dividends from India treasury only. Each dividend pays £1 per firm share plus £1 to the manager; with manager consent a shareholder may forgo payment for any number of shares. Record total actual cash paid out as the dividend marker, then sweep remaining India money to London.
